tripadvisor_description: Vaishno Devi, also known as Mata Rani, Trikuta and Vaishnavi, is a manifestation of the Hindu Mother Goddess of MahaKali, MahaSaraswati and MahaLakshmi.
review_1: It was probably my 10th visit to the holy shrine, the last one being over 8 years ago. I began the climb at 1610 hrs and the weather was very good. As I am a veteran, I had access to the Armed Forces facilities and my entry slip #0033 was made in advance. A  young colleague accompanied me to the starting point and I could save some time here. A photograph was taken prior to commencement of the climb in the army camp. Being in a hurry, I took only two five minutes breaks and used a climb of 360 stairs once. I had taken the conventional route on which ponies /horses, palanquins and carts are permitted. The entire route is full of eateries, some restaurants, cafes. Simian species are  plentiful, but were not seen to attack pilgrims. Post -Ardhkumari one can't use equine species. The view and the lights were awesome. There is a metallic grill on valley side of the route. Toilet facilities are adequate. One needs to be careful. Battery operated cars are available  if online booking is done. I was lucky to get a VIP darshan and quickly made my way back.  The environment is amazing . As  I began the downhill journey after the best darshan ever, I was mor observant and saw devotees young ,old, children, men and women moving towards the shrine as if pulled by a magnetic force. Post -Ardhkumari I took the Trikutta route down which was only for people wanting to walk up/down and was much quieter and with less gradient albeit a little longer.  I had some food in one 'langar' around 3 kms from the end of the descent. It is at a totally different point.  With some difficulty, I could get a cab to my hotel. All  pilgrims must factor the fact that prepaid sims from other parts of India can't be used in J &K.  I would strongly recommend a visit to the shrine for both religious and fitness aspects.
review_2: My Vaishno Devi helicopter yatra in 2026 was smooth, well organized, and truly peaceful. HelicopterBooking.org booking process was transparent, the journey time was short, and the overall atmosphere felt calm despite the crowd. Staff coordination at Katra and Sanjichhat was disciplined and helpful. This experience is especially ideal for families, senior citizens, and anyone seeking a comfortable and time saving yatra.

It is Located on the banks of Dal Lake, Hazratbal Mosque is considered to be the holiest Muslim shrine in Kashmir. Hazratbal is a white-domed mosque at the heart of the main university area of Srinagar.
The shrine has a relic called the Moi-e-Muqqadas, which is believed to be a hair of the Prophet Muhammad. As per a legend, a descendant of the Prophet Muhammad, Syed Abdullah, brought the relic to India. Later, the relic was inherited by Syed Abdullah’s son, Syed Hamid, who sold it to a Kashmiri businessman after he was stripped of his family estate and was unable to care for the relic. Aurangzeb captured the businessman, Khwaja Nur-ud-Din Eshai and seized the relic. Upon realizing his mistake, Aurangzeb gave it back to the businessman. The relic finally reached Kashmir in 1700 and Khwaja Nur-ud-Din Eshai’s daughter established a shrine for the relic.
Presently, the relic is kept in a glass case inside the mosque and is displayed on the holy days like Shab-e-Meraj.

The journey to Shey Monastery itself is an adventure, as you wind through the rugged terrain, passing by serene valleys and shimmering rivers. My visit took an unexpected turn as we ended up approaching the monastery from behind, unaware of the main entrance. This led us to a series of mini stairs that zigzagged their way up the hillside.

Hiking up those narrow, winding stairs was an unexpected thrill. The ascent was exciting and a little bit scary, but it added an extra layer of adventure to our visit. As we climbed higher, the anticipation grew, and the view of the surrounding landscape became increasingly captivating.

Upon reaching the main courtyard, I was immediately struck by the sense of tranquility and serenity that enveloped the place. The main entrance, with its whitewashed walls and traditional Tibetan architecture, was a sight to behold. Prayer flags fluttered in the breeze overhead, enhancing the spiritual atmosphere.

One of the highlights of the visit was the giant copper statue of Lord Buddha. The sense of reverence in the prayer hall is profound, and you can witness the locals and pilgrims offering their prayers with utmost devotion.

Shey Monastery also offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. I recommend climbing up to the monastery's upper levels for an unobstructed view of the Indus Valley below. The sight of the river meandering through the valley and the distant snow-capped peaks is a sight that will stay with you forever.

While the monastery is a spiritual haven, it is essential to be respectful of the monks and the local customs. Dress modestly and maintain a quiet demeanor as a sign of respect for this sacred place.

Shey Monastery is a must-visit destination for anyone traveling to Ladakh. It offers a unique opportunity to connect with the spiritual essence of the region while being surrounded by awe-inspiring natural beauty. I left Shey Monastery with a sense of inner peace and gratitude, making it one of the most memorable stops on my Ladakh journey.

review_1: The Thiksey Monastery or the Thiksey Gompa is a Buddhist Monastery located on top of a Hill in Thiksey approximately 19 kilometers east of Leh, in the Ladakh Region. This Monastery has a High Exuberant Statue of Maitreya Buddha which was built recently in 1980s. The Thiksay Monastery is famous for the Morning Prayers conducted every day, where Tourists can also go and try to resonate with the Spiritual Vibe. A Good Place to visit and Great Views to enjoy as well.

SPITUK GONPA
SPETHUB (EXAMPLARY )
POPULARLY KNOWN AS THE SPITUK GONPA IS ONE OF THE PROMINENT GE-LUG-PA MONASTERIES. IT WAS FOUNDED BY KING GRAS-PA-BUM- LDE IN THE LAST 14th CENTURY.A.D. THE SITE FOR THE MONASTERY WAS GRANTED BY THE KING TO THE TWO EMISARIES SENT BY TSONG KHA PA FOR INSTALLATION OF THE STATUE OF TSE-PAG-MED WHICH IS SAID TO HAVE CRIGINATED FROM THE NOSE BLOOD OF TSONG-KHA-PA. THE STATUE WAS INSTALLED WITHIN THE 10 FEET HIGH STATUE OF BUDDHA IN THE ASSEMBLY HALL OF THE MONASTERY. IN THE MAIN TEMPLE, AT THE UPPER END THERE ARE THE SEAT FOR HIS HOLINESS THE DALAI LAMA & BAKULA RINPOCHEY. IT ALSO HOUSE THE STATUES OF SHAKYAMUNI. TSONG-KHA PA & HIS TWO DISCIPILES. YAMANTAKA & AVALOKITESVARA. THERE ARE THE KANGYUR & TANGYUR (THE SCRIPTURES & COMMENTARIES) IN WOODEN SHELVES ON THE LEFT OF THE HALL & PANTINGS OF THE PROTECTOR DEITIES ON THE WALLS. THE CHOW KHANG ON THE UPPER FLOOR HOUSE THE STATUE OF THE CHOW IN THE CENTRAL POSITION BROUGHT FROM TIBET IN 1960. A STATUE OF PADMA SAMBHAVA TO ITS RIGHT & A SILVER PLATED CHANG-CHUB-CHORTEN TO THE LEFT. 
TO THE RIGHT OF CHOW-KHANG IS DOLMA LAKHANG WHICH HOUSES TWENTY ONE COPPER GIFT TARAS. EACH TARA HOLD A LONG STEMMED LOTUS & HAS SEVEN EYES (EYES OF KNOWLEDGE) THESE STATUES WERE ALSO BROUGHT FROM TIBET BY THE PRESENT INCARANATE LAMA. THE STATUES OF DOLMA IS WORSHIPPED IN ALL THE MONASTERIES IRRESPECTIVE OF DIFFERENT SECTS & THE HYMNS OF DOLMA ARE RECITED DAILY BY MONKS & LAYMEN ALIKE. THE CHIKHANG BELOW THE MAIN
MONASTERY HOUSES THE STATUES OF LORD BUDDHA, WITH HIS TWO DISCIPLES & YAMANTAKA. THERE ARE PAINTINGS OF THE PROTECTOR DEITIES ON THE WALLS.
THE INNER TEMPLE CONTAIN SEVERAL PRECIOUS STATUES & CHAM SRING, THE PROTECTOR DEITY OF MONASTERY. SPITUK GUSTOR, THE ANNUAL MONASTIC FESTIVAL TAKES PLACE FROM THE 26th TO 28th OF THE 11th TIBETAN MONTH.
BY COURTESY OF TOURISM DEV. AUTHORITY LEH

review_3:
This monastery, like many others in the region, rests atop a small hill. Vehicles can conveniently reach the base of the monastery, and there is no entry fee. However, a significant climb up numerous stairs awaits visitors.
The main gompa can be accessed through a room where a monk engages in routine prayers. The face of the deity is covered, adding a sense of reverence to the environment. What sets this monastery apart is its exceptional vantage point offering a stunning view of Leh airport. Visitors can clearly witness the landing and takeoff of airplanes, adding a unique and captivating element to the monastery visit. The combination of spiritual ambiance and the scenic view makes this monastery a distinctive stop in the region.
